mainTopic: Uncertain קידושין between two sisters: when גט, חליצה and יבום are required, and why each clause of the משנה is needed
overview: This amud deals with a man who betrothed one of two sisters but does not know which one. Since a man may not be married to two sisters, he must give a גט to both. If he dies, his brothers face the same doubt about יבום. With one brother, that brother does חליצה with both sisters. With two brothers, one does חליצה and then the other may do יבום. The משנה then works through two men who each betrothed one of two sisters, with different numbers of brothers on each side. The גמרא first tries to prove that קידושין that can never lead to living together still count. It rejects the proof: the sisters were known at first and only mixed up later, as the wording 'he does not know' shows. It then explains why each clause of the משנה is needed: the order of חליצה before יבום, and the decrees the rabbis chose not to make. The amud ends by comparing our case to a משנה of four brothers married to two sisters, and the difference between them is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: One man betrothed one of two sisters and does not know which
steps.stepSummary: A man who betrothed one of two sisters, without knowing which, must give a גט to each of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man betrothed one of two sisters and does not know which one he betrothed, he gives a bill of divorce to this one and a bill of divorce to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a case of doubt: a man made קידושין with one of two sisters but forgot which one. It rules that he must divorce both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot marry either sister, because she might be the sister of his wife, and one may not marry his wife's sister. Since either one might really be his wife, each needs a גט to be free to marry someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
He betrothed (made קידושין)
Sisters
A bill of divorce

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who betrothed
one of two sisters,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ אֵי זֹה מֵהֶן קִידֵּשׁ —
phrases.english: and does not know which of them he betrothed —
gives a bill of divorce to this one and a bill of divorce to that one.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unknown which sister was betrothed, the man gives a גט to both.

steps.title: He died leaving one brother
steps.stepSummary: If the man died before divorcing and left one brother, that brother does חליצה with both sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died and he had one brother, that brother performs חליצה with both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same case: now the husband died with no children, and the question is what his single brother does. The answer is חליצה with both sisters, not יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one sister is truly the brother's יבמה, and the other is the sister of a woman tied to him by זיקה, so she is forbidden to him. Since he does not know which is which, he cannot do יבום with either one, so he releases both with חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Performs חליצה, the release ceremony instead of יבום
To both of them
Brother

phrases.english: If he died and he had one brother —
he performs חליצה with both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same doubt to the case where the husband died
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single brother must do חליצה with both sisters and may not do יבום with either.

steps.title: He died leaving two brothers
steps.stepSummary: With two brothers, one does חליצה with one sister and the other may then do יבום with the other sister. If they married without asking first, they are not forced apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had two brothers, one performs חליצה and one performs יבום. If they went ahead and married, we do not take the women away from them.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the dead man has two brothers, and the משנה shows how one of the sisters can end up in יבום. It also adds that if the brothers married the sisters on their own, the court does not separate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First one brother does חליצה with one sister, which removes the doubt about the זיקה. After that, the other sister is either the real יבמה or a woman not tied to the family at all, so the second brother may marry her. The order matters: חליצה comes first, then יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Performs יבום (levirate marriage)
They went ahead and married (without asking first)
We do not take them out of their hands, meaning they are not forced to divorce

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think both brothers may simply do יבום with one sister each from the start. The משנה's plan is חליצה first; the 'קדמו וכנסו' line only says that after the fact we do not separate them.

phrases.english: If he had two brothers —
one performs חליצה and one performs יבום.
If they went ahead and married —
we do not take the women away from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the number of brothers from one to two, which allows יבום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two brothers, one does חליצה and the other may do יבום; if both married on their own, they are not separated.

steps.title: Two men betrothed two sisters and neither knows which
steps.stepSummary: Two different men each betrothed one of two sisters, and neither knows which one is his. Each man gives a גט to both sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two men betrothed two sisters. This one does not know which he betrothed, and that one does not know which he betrothed. This one gives two bills of divorce, and that one gives two bills of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new, harder case: two unrelated men, two sisters, and neither man knows which sister is his wife. Each man must give a גט to both sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sister might be married to either man, so neither man can live with either woman. To fully free both women, each man gives two גיטין, one to each sister.

keyTerms.meaning: Two men who betrothed
Bills of divorce (plural of גט)

phrases.english: Two men who betrothed two sisters,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אֵי זוֹ קִידֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: this one does not know which one he betrothed,
and that one does not know which one he betrothed —
this one gives two bills of divorce,
and that one gives two bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from one man with a doubt to two men with a doubt
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the two men gives a גט to both sisters.

steps.title: Both men died, each leaving one brother
steps.stepSummary: If both men died and each left one brother, each brother does חליצה with both sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they died, and this one had a brother and that one had a brother, this brother performs חליצה with both of them, and that brother performs חליצה with both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the two-men case, the משנה rules for when each dead man left only one brother. Each brother must do חליצה with both sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother does not know which sister is his יבמה, and the other sister may be forbidden to him as the sister of his זקוקה. So, just like in step 2, neither brother can do יבום, and each must release both women.

keyTerms.meaning: They died
This one had a brother and that one had a brother

phrases.english: If they died, and this one had a brother and that one had a brother —
this brother performs חליצה with both of them,
and that brother performs חליצה with both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the one-brother rule of step 2 to the two-men case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each single brother does חליצה with both sisters.

steps.title: One man left one brother and the other left two
steps.stepSummary: The single brother does חליצה with both sisters. Of the two brothers, one does חליצה and the other may do יבום. If they married on their own, they are not separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this one had one brother and that one had two, the single brother performs חליצה with both of them, and of the two brothers, one performs חליצה and one performs יבום. If they went ahead and married, we do not take the women away from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה mixes the earlier rules: the side with one brother follows step 2, and the side with two brothers follows step 3. It repeats that after-the-fact marriages are not undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lone brother still cannot do יבום, so he releases both sisters. The family with two brothers can use the step 3 method: one brother's חליצה clears the doubt of אחות זקוקה. Once the lone brother of the other family has also done חליצה, the other brother may marry the remaining sister. Until then she might still be the other family's יבמה, a יבמה לשוק, as the גמרא explains later (step 21).

keyTerms.meaning: The single one (the lone brother)
And the two (the pair of brothers)

phrases.english: If this one had one brother and that one had two —
the single brother performs חליצה with both of them,
and of the two brothers — one performs חליצה,
and one performs יבום.
If they went ahead and married, we do not take the women away from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the one-brother and two-brother rules within the two-men case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lone brother does חליצה with both; of the pair, one does חליצה and one may do יבום.

steps.title: Each man left two brothers
steps.stepSummary: One brother from each family does חליצה with a different sister. Then the second brother of each family may do יבום with the woman who did חליצה with the other family's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this one had two brothers and that one had two brothers, the brother of this one performs חליצה with one sister, and the brother of that one performs חליצה with one sister. The brother of this one performs יבום with the woman who did חליצה with that one, and the brother of that one performs יבום with the woman who did חליצה with this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the case where both families have two brothers. It gives a criss-cross plan that lets both sisters end up in יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say sister A did חליצה with family 1's brother, and sister B did חליצה with family 2's brother. Now family 1's second brother may marry B: if B was family 1's widow, family 2's חליצה with her did nothing and this is a real יבום; if B was family 2's widow, she is already released and is just a permitted woman to him. The same logic works for family 2's second brother marrying A.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman who did חליצה with him (his חלוצה)
With one (of the sisters)
The brother of this one

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה rests on one idea: a brother may not do יבום when the woman might be the sister of his זקוקה. A single brother must do חליצה with both sisters, but once a חליצה clears the doubt, another brother may safely do יבום.
steps.confusionAlert: Each family's brother does יבום with the woman who did חליצה with the OTHER family, not with his own brother's חלוצה, which would be forbidden.

phrases.english: If this one had two brothers and that one had two —
the brother of this one performs חליצה with one sister,
and the brother of that one performs חליצה with one sister.

phrases.aramaic: אָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה מְיַיבֵּם חֲלוּצָתוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: The brother of this one performs יבום with the חלוצה of that one,
phrases.notes: This is the second brother of the family, not the one who just did חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה מְיַיבֵּם חֲלוּצָתוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.
phrases.english: and the brother of that one performs יבום with the חלוצה of this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final and most complex case in the series, with two brothers on each side
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One brother from each family does חליצה with a different sister; then each family's other brother may do יבום with the other family's חלוצה.

steps.title: If two brothers did חליצה first, the other two may not both do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends: if two brothers of one family went ahead and did חליצה, the other two brothers cannot both do יבום. One does חליצה and one may do יבום. If they married on their own, they are not separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two went ahead and did חליצה, the two may not both do יבום. Rather, one does חליצה and one does יבום. If they went ahead and married, we do not take the wives away from them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It covers a case where some brothers acted before asking בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after one family's brothers did חליצה, the other family still has a problem. If both of its brothers did יבום, one of them might be marrying the sister of the woman bound to him. So one must do חליצה first. Only then may the other do יבום. But if they already married, בית דין does not force them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: They went ahead, acting before asking בית דין
Does חליצה, the ceremony that frees the widow from יבום
Does יבום, marrying the brother's widow
We do not take the wives away from them

phrases.english: If two went ahead and performed חליצה
phrases.notes: These are the two brothers of one family. The rest of the line is about what the other family's two brothers may do.

phrases.english: the two may not both do יבום,
rather, one does חליצה and one does יבום.
If they went ahead and married,
we do not take the wives away from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case of two families of brothers from Step 7, for when brothers acted before asking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If two brothers already did חליצה, the other two may not both do יבום. One does חליצה and then the other may do יבום. If they married anyway, they are not separated.

steps.title: A proof that a betrothal that can never lead to marriage still counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by suggesting that the משנה proves something: קידושין that can never lead to living together are still real קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Learn from this that a betrothal that cannot lead to living together is still a betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by drawing a big lesson from the משנה. It says the משנה proves that a betrothal which can never be completed is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man cannot marry either sister, because each one might be the sister of his wife. So his קידושין can never lead to marriage. Yet the משנה makes him give a גט to both sisters. That suggests the קידושין took effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; a lesson drawn from a source
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Able to lead to living together as husband and wife

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about the brothers here. It goes back to the opening case of the משנה, where one man betrothed one of two sisters and must give a גט to both (Step 1). The two-men case gets its own, separate proof attempt later (Step 14).

phrases.english: גמרא: Learn from this:
betrothals that cannot lead to living together
are still betrothals!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁאֵין מְסוּרִין לְבִיאָה הָווּ קִדּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by drawing a general rule from the case in Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה are valid קידושין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה requires a גט for both sisters even though neither can ever be married

steps.title: The sisters were known at first and only mixed up later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה is talking about a case where, when he betrothed her, he knew which sister she was. They got mixed up only afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are we dealing here? With a case where they were recognized at first and later got mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the משנה's case is different from what we assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he knew exactly whom he was betrothing, the קידושין could lead to marriage when they were made. The mix-up came only later. So this case says nothing about קידושין that could never lead to marriage from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? Used to narrow down the case
They were recognized, known apart
They got mixed up

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
When they were recognized, and in the end got mixed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 9 by redefining the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the קידושין were unclear from the start. Really, they were clear at the time and only became unclear later.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports the mixed-up-later reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading from the משנה's exact words. It says 'he does not know', not 'it is not known', so the matter was known at some point.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is precise too, because it says 'and he does not know' and not 'and it is not known.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new reading by looking closely at the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He does not know' describes his present confusion. That fits a case where he once knew and later forgot. 'It is not known' would mean it was never known at all. The משנה chose the first wording, which fits Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is precise too; a support taken from exact wording
And he does not know
And it is not known

steps.whatToRemember: The proof about קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה falls away. The משנה is about sisters who were known at the time of קידושין and only got mixed up later.

phrases.english: The wording is precise too, as it teaches:
'and he does not know,'
and it does not teach: 'and it is not known.'
phrases.notes: 'He doesn't know' sounds like he forgot. 'It isn't known' would mean nobody ever knew.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 10 with proof from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the sisters were known at first and mixed up later
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ' rather than 'וְאֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ'

steps.title: Then what is the first clause teaching us
steps.stepSummary: If the קידושין were clearly valid, then of course the man must give a גט to both sisters. So what new thing does that clause teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Now that the case is a simple one, the rule of giving two גיטין seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קידושין were valid, and we do not know which sister is his wife. So he obviously must divorce both. Without the proof from Step 9, that clause seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? Asked when a rule seems obvious

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: This is asked about the rule that the man gives a גט to both sisters, which now seems obvious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion of Steps 10 and 11: if the case is simple, the clause seems unneeded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause of the משנה that requires a גט for each sister (Step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the קידושין were clearly valid and only later mixed up, giving a גט to both sisters is obvious. So why does the משנה need to say it?

steps.title: The first clause sets up the last clause: חליצה before יבום
steps.stepSummary: The first clause is there for the sake of the last clause. That clause teaches that when there are two brothers, one must do חליצה first. Only after that may the other do יבום, because doing יבום first would mean marrying the sister of a woman bound to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part was needed: if he died and had one brother, that brother does חליצה with both. If he had two, one does חליצה and one does יבום. It must be חליצה first and then יבום. יבום first is not allowed, because he would be marrying the sister of the woman bound to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The first clause is just the setup, and the real new teaching is in the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the חליצה, one of the sisters is bound to both brothers, and nobody knows which. If one brother did יבום first, he might marry the sister of the woman tied to him, which is forbidden. Once his brother has done חליצה with one sister, that bond is gone. Then the other sister may be taken in יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
It was needed for him; it had to be taught
Specifically, only this way
The sister of the woman bound to him for יבום

steps.whatToRemember: The order matters: חליצה first, then יבום. Doing יבום first would mean marrying the sister of a woman still tied to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה needs every clause. It also sets a practical rule for the order of חליצה and יבום when sisters are involved.

phrases.english: The last clause was what he needed:
if he died and had one brother,
he does חליצה with both of them;
if he had two brothers,
one does חליצה and one does יבום.
Specifically, first doing חליצה and then doing יבום,
but doing יבום first, no,
because he would come upon the sister of the woman bound to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 12 by pointing to the last clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The clause is needed to set up a later clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause seemed to teach nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause sets up the last clause. That clause teaches that חליצה must come before יבום, so no brother marries the sister of a woman bound to him.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה of two men and two sisters and drawing a proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about two men who betrothed two sisters and suggests it proves that קידושין which can never lead to living together are still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Two men who betrothed two sisters, and so on.' Learn from here that קידושין which cannot lead to living together are real קידושין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and right away tries to learn a rule from it. This is the same move it made a moment ago with the case of one man and two sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither man knows which sister is his, so neither can ever live with either sister, because she might be the other man's wife. Even so, the משנה requires each man to give a גט to both sisters, which looks like it treats the קידושין as real.

keyTerms.meaning: two sisters
betrothal that can never lead to living together as husband and wife
learn from this

phrases.english: Two who betrothed two sisters, etc.
Learn from this:
betrothals that cannot lead to living together
are valid betrothals!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: קִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁאֵין מְסוּרִין לְבִיאָה הָווּ קִדּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the proof attempt of Step 9, this time with the משנה's second case.
steps.raayaObject: קידושין that can never lead to living together are valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that each man gives a גט to both sisters.

steps.title: The sisters were known at first and mixed up later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: here too, each man knew whom he betrothed, and the sisters got mixed up only afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where they were known at first and only later got mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof with the same answer it gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each man knew his wife at the moment of קידושין, then the קידושין could lead to living together when they were made. The later mix-up does not cancel them, so the case proves nothing about קידושין that were blocked from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: they were recognized, known
they got mixed up

phrases.english: Here too, it is when they were recognized
and in the end were mixed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from this clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the sisters were never identified. The case may be one where they were known at the time of קידושין.

steps.title: The wording 'he does not know' supports the rejection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading: the משנה says 'he does not know', not 'it is not known', which suggests it was known at first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too, since it teaches 'and he does not know' and does not teach 'and it is not known.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its narrow reading by pointing to the exact words of the משנה, and then closes the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He does not know' describes a person who lost track of something. 'It is not known' would mean nobody ever knew. The משנה chose the first, so it fits a case where the sisters were once known.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is exact too, it supports this
he does not know (now)
it is not known (by anyone, ever)

phrases.english: It is exact too, since it teaches:
'and he does not know,'
and it does not teach 'and it is not known.'
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 15 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: The case is one where the sisters were known at first and mixed up later.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's word choice: 'he does not know' rather than 'it is not known'.

steps.title: Then what is this clause teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If the קידושין were clearly valid, it is obvious that each man must give two גיטין. What does the clause add?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the case is clearly valid קידושין, the גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man surely married one of the sisters, and he does not know which. Of course he must divorce both to be safe, so the clause seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it teaching us?

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The narrow reading from Steps 15–16 makes the clause look unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause that each man gives two גיטין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the קידושין are known to be valid, giving both sisters a גט out of doubt is obvious, so the clause seems needless.

steps.title: The first clause is there for the later clause about the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The first clause was needed as a lead-in to the later clause: if the men died, one with a single brother and one with two brothers, the single brother does חליצה to both, and of the two brothers, one does חליצה and one does יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later clause was what it needed: if the men died, one leaving one brother and the other leaving two, the single brother does חליצה with both sisters, and of the two brothers, one does חליצה and one does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first clause only sets the scene. The real new teaching is the later clause about what the dead men's brothers do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single brother cannot do יבום with either sister, since she might be the other man's widow, and then she is forbidden to him. So he does חליצה with both. In the family with two brothers, one does חליצה with one sister, and then the other may do יבום with the other sister. Step 21 explains why the order matters.

keyTerms.meaning: the later clause
it was needed
does חליצה, the ceremony that frees the widow from יבום
does יבום, marries his brother's childless widow

phrases.english: The later clause was what it needed:
if they died, and this one had one and this one had two
phrases.notes: 'One' and 'two' mean brothers. Each dead husband left brothers who are bound to his widow.

phrases.english: the single brother does חליצה with both of them,
and of the two, one does חליצה and one does יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The obvious clause sets the scene for a later clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause seemed to teach something obvious all by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the background needed for the later ruling about the brothers.

steps.title: But the brothers' rule is the same as the earlier case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the later clause is also obvious, because it is the same rule as the earlier case.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious; this is the same as the first clause!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The later clause also seems to repeat something the משנה already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case of one man and two sisters already taught that when there are two brothers, one does חליצה and one does יבום. So it seems the later clause adds nothing new either.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious
this is the same as the first clause

phrases.english: That is obvious; this is the first clause!
phrases.notes: He means the earlier case of one man and two sisters, where two brothers also split into חליצה and יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The later clause about the two brothers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule about two brothers already appears in the earlier clause, so repeating it seems needless.

steps.title: No גזירה forbidding two brothers because of one
steps.stepSummary: The clause is needed, because one might think the rabbis would forbid יבום for the two brothers because of the single brother, who may not do יבום. The משנה teaches they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a גזירה for the two brothers because of the one brother. So it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is new in the later clause. Here the two kinds of family sit side by side, one family with one brother and one with two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single brother may only do חליצה. Since both families are in the same story, one might fear people would mix them up, so the two brothers should also be limited to חליצה. The משנה teaches that no such גזירה was made, and one of the two may still do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said
let us make a protective rabbinic rule
two because of one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the two brothers are like the earlier case for no reason. The new point is that the single brother's limit is not carried over to the two brothers.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us make a גזירה about two because of one,
phrases.notes: The two brothers would be stopped from יבום because the single brother in the other family cannot do יבום.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לִיגְזוֹר תְּרֵי אַטּוּ חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point, no גזירה, that the earlier clause could not teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the single brother may only do חליצה, the rabbis might forbid יבום for the two brothers too.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה was made, so one of the two brothers may do יבום.

steps.title: חליצה must come first, or he may marry another man's יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The rule works only if one brother does חליצה first and the other does יבום after. Doing יבום first is forbidden, since he may be marrying a woman still bound to the other family's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only when one does חליצה and then the other does יבום. But doing יבום first is not allowed, because he might be marrying a יבמה who is forbidden to outsiders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit on the order: first חליצה, then יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before any חליצה, each sister may be the widow of the other family. If one brother does יבום first, the woman he marries may really be bound to the single brother of the other family, and until he frees her she is forbidden to everyone else. Once the חליצה frees that link, the יבום is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: specifically, only
run into, come up against a prohibition
a יבמה marrying an outsider before she is freed, which is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of two men and two sisters, the קידושין are valid only because the sisters were known at first. If one dead husband left one brother and the other left two, the single brother does חליצה with both. Of the two brothers, one does חליצה first, and only then may the other do יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: In the parallel case of one man, doing יבום first was a problem of the sister of a woman bound to him. Here the danger is different: marrying a woman who may be someone else's יבמה.

phrases.english: And this is specifically doing חליצה and then doing יבום,
but doing יבום first, no,
because he runs into the prohibition of a יבמה to an outsider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the required order for the rule allowed in Steps 18–20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the two brothers, חליצה must come before יבום. יבום first is forbidden because of יבמה לשוק.

steps.title: Why teach the case where each man has two brothers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's clause about each man having two brothers and asks why it is needed, since it seems to be the same as the earlier rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If this one had two brothers and that one had two brothers, and so on.' Why do I need this too? It is the same as that earlier case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and challenges it as repeating what was already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier clause, one man left one brother and the other left two, and we already learned that one of the two brothers may do יבום after חליצה. Here both men left two brothers, so one brother in each family can do יבום. The same principle seems to apply, so the clause looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this as well?
This is the same as that
And so on, meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: If this one had two and that one had two, etc.
phrases.notes: He means two brothers each. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the line in the משנה.

phrases.english: Why do I need this as well?
This is the same as that!
phrases.notes: 'That' is the earlier clause, where one man had one brother and the other had two (step 18).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הַיְינוּ הָךְ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'why is this clause needed' challenges on the same משנה, now on its final clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about each dead man having two brothers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the rule follows from the earlier clause, so it should not need to be stated.

steps.title: No decree against יבום in case it is done before חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The clause is needed. Otherwise one might think the rabbis would ban יבום entirely, in case someone does יבום before חליצה. The משנה teaches they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let the rabbis make a decree, in case someone does יבום without חליצה being done first. So the משנה teaches us that they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the clause is not repetitive. It rules out a possible rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both families have two brothers, each family has someone ready to do יבום. That raises the worry that one of them will rush ahead before the needed חליצה in the other family has been done. One might think this risk calls for a ban, but the משנה shows the rabbis made no such decree.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Let them make a rabbinic decree
Perhaps, in case
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The last clause teaches that the rabbis did not ban יבום out of fear that it would be done before חליצה. The correct order is still required: חליצה first, then יבום.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Let them make a decree, in case
he does יבום without חליצה,
phrases.notes: He means doing יבום before the חליצה that must come first, the wrong order described in step 21.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לִיגְזוֹר דִּלְמָא מְיַיבֵּם בְּלֹא חֲלִיצָה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out a possible decree (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rabbis would forbid יבום in case someone does it before the required חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such decree was made. One brother in each family may do יבום, as long as the order is kept.

steps.title: Why is this different from four brothers married to two sisters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts this case with a משנה where two sisters, widowed from two of four brothers, may only do חליצה and never יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned in a משנה: four brothers, two of whom were married to two sisters, and the two married to the sisters died. Those sisters do חליצה but do not do יבום. Why not say the same here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling by pointing to another משנה, where sisters are not allowed to do יבום at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the four-brother case, each sister is bound to each remaining brother, so she is the sister of a woman bound to him, and יבום is forbidden. Here too the two women are sisters, and both may be bound to the same brothers. So why is יבום allowed here, after חליצה?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
They do חליצה
They enter into יבום

steps.confusionAlert: In the four-brother case the sisters can never do יבום, not even after the other sister has done חליצה. That is exactly why it seems to contradict our משנה.

phrases.english: What is different from what we learned:
Four brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and the ones married to the sisters died —
these women do חליצה
and do not do יבום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from asking why the clause is needed to challenging the ruling itself with a contrasting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one brother may do יבום after the other family's brother has done חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction from a parallel case: sisters bound to the same brothers cannot do יבום there, so they should not be able to here either.

steps.title: The two cases cannot be compared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison outright. The explanation of the difference comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge and says the cases are not alike. This line sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This exclamation signals that the comparison in step 24 is flawed. The גמרא has not yet said why. The explanation of what makes the two cases different comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: How can these be compared?! (a strong rejection of a comparison)

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison raised in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between our משנה and the משנה of four brothers married to two sisters.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases are claimed to be fundamentally different. The specific difference is explained in the following lines.
